```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(tigris)

# 1. Load the main New Orleans dataset
nola_data <- readRDS("nola_data.rds")

# 2. Re-create category filtering and inclusion rule
restaurant_categories <- nola_data |>
  filter(!is.na(categories)) |>
  separate_rows(categories, sep = ",") |>
  mutate(category = str_to_lower(str_trim(categories))) |>
  filter(category != "")

target_cats <- c("bakery", "desserts", "ice cream & frozen yogurt")

selected_business_ids <- restaurant_categories |>
  filter(category %in% target_cats) |>
  distinct(business_id)

selected_businesses <- nola_data |>
  inner_join(selected_business_ids, by = "business_id")

# 3. Re-create geo_summary for Figure 1
global_avg_stars <- mean(selected_businesses$stars, na.rm = TRUE)

geo_summary <- selected_businesses |>
  filter(!is.na(postal_code) & postal_code != "") |>
  group_by(postal_code) |>
  summarize(
    Restaurants = n(),
    avg_stars = round(mean(stars, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    total_reviews = sum(review_count, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_reviews = round(mean(review_count, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    adjusted_score = round(
      (sum(review_count * stars) + 50 * global_avg_stars) / (sum(review_count) + 50), 2
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  filter(Restaurants > 0) |>
  arrange(desc(Restaurants))
```

## Figure 1 
The bar chart highlights which postal codes contain the highest concentration of sweet treat businesses in New Orleans.

```{r}
#| label: fig-postal-count
#| fig.cap: "Number of Sweet Treat Restaurants by Postal Code"

geo_summary |>
  slice_head(n = 10) |>
  mutate(postal_code = fct_reorder(postal_code, Restaurants)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = Restaurants, y = postal_code, fill = Restaurants)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "C") +
  labs(
    title = "Top Postal Codes for Sweet Treats in New Orleans",
    subtitle = "Ranked by total number of qualifying establishments",
    x = "Number of Restaurants",
    y = "Postal Code"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )
```

##Figure 2 
The box plot compares the spread of Yelp star ratings across your different postal zones or categories.

```{r}
#| label: fig-ratings-dist
#| fig.cap: "Distribution of Star Ratings Across Postal Zones"

selected_businesses |>
  filter(!is.na(postal_code) & postal_code != "") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(postal_code, stars, FUN = median), y = stars, fill = postal_code)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.2, size = 1.5, alpha = 0.5, color = "black") +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "plasma") +
  labs(
    title = "Star Rating Distribution by Postal Code",
    subtitle = "Individual points represent unique restaurants",
    x = "Postal Code",
    y = "Yelp Star Rating"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )
```

### Figure 3

This scatter plot examines whether restaurants with higher star ratings also tend to accumulate more reviews (or if smaller niche spots punch above their weight).

```{r}
#| label: fig-reviews-vs-stars
#| fig.cap: "Relationship Between Review Volume and Star Ratings"

selected_businesses |>
  filter(review_count < 500) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = review_count, y = stars)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = review_count), alpha = 0.7, size = 2.5) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, color = "darkorange", linetype = "dashed", se = FALSE) +
  scale_color_viridis_c(option = "viridis") +
  labs(
    title = "Review Volume vs. Star Rating",
    subtitle = "Checking for rating bias among high-volume establishments",
    x = "Total Review Count",
    y = "Average Star Rating",
    color = "Review\nCount"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )
```
